attributes.probed_form:
PROBE P1 (REVERTED, BUILD-ABORTED, and the abort IS the measurement): inserted `#pragma opt_propagation reset` on the line immediately after add_vmu_file's closing brace (memcard.c:311), scoping the L267 `off` to add_vmu_file alone. add_vmu_file's own webfrank pin HELD (`WEBFRANK add_vmu_file: adjusted 5 instruction atoms/fields`), proving the tight scope preserved the bracketed function exactly. The build then ABORTED at the next pin: `ValueError: memCardErrorPrompt: input hash 908240734fbd... != expected eb4f114353ce...`. READ: turning propagation back ON changes memCardErrorPrompt's compiled body, i.e. the leak is load-bearing for a function that is currently byte-exact. MemCardCreateGaunt was never reached, so its status was unknown after P1.

PROBE P2 (REVERTED, REGRESSED, and this is the full-roster measurement): PIN-COMPATIBLE re-scope. Kept `opt_propagation off` in force across all three pinned functions and turned it ON everywhere else, by adding two more bracket pairs: `#pragma opt_propagation off` before `int MemCardCreateGaunt(int port, int slot)` with `#pragma opt_propagation reset` after its closing brace, and the same pair around `s32 memCardErrorPrompt(const char* msg)`. All three pins then HELD and the object built, so every one of the 27 unpinned functions was measured with propagation ON against a baseline with it OFF. Result: FIVE regressions, ZERO improvements, net real +622 across the TU.
